title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 360
paragraphs: Among the Greeks, Heracles, Dionysos, and Pan are reckoned the latest-born of the gods; but for the Egyptians, Pan is a very ancient god and is one of those known as the eight gods, while Heracles belongs to the second rank, called the twelve gods, and Dionysos is of the third rank, those born from the twelve gods. Now as to Heracles I have already shown how many years old he is according to the Egyptians themselves, reckoning down to the reign of Amasis; Pan is said to have existed even longer than these, while Dionysos is given the fewest years in comparison to the others, and even for him they count fifteen thousand years down to the reign of Amasis. The Egyptians say they know this for certain, since they have always kept records and written down the years as they passed. Now the Dionysos said to have been born of Semele daughter of Cadmos was born about sixteen hundred years before my time; Heracles, son of Alcmene, about nine hundred years; and the Pan born of Penelope — for the Greeks say Pan was born of her and Hermes — came into being after the Trojan Wars, about eight hundred years before my time.
